cluster_stories.title: RSI Control: Can AI Models Perform Covert Sabotage in the Self-Improvement Process?
cluster_stories.summary: arXiv:2610.27735v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recursive self-improvement, in which frontier AI models work on training the next generation, is quickly becoming a reality. However, the safety of this process has received far less attention than it should. A misaligned model training its successor can shape what that successor knows, how it behaves, and what it wants, and the harm carries forward into the next generation. We study this risk through the lens of AI control. We introduce RSI Control Arena, a testbed in which a frontier model, acting as an autonomous R\&D agent, is given a benign main task from a stage of a successor model's training pipeline together with a covert side task to install a misaligned property in the successor. The testbed contains 16 side tasks in three classes, forming 22 task pairs with main tasks that span the pipeline from data curation to reinforcement learning. We evaluate six frontier models as agents against LLM monitors that read the transcript
cluster_stories.headline: RSI CONTROL: AI Models Can Sabotage Self-Improvement Process

cluster_stories.title: ‘These risks are real’: the threat of AI bioweapons – podcast
cluster_stories.summary: In his annual speech on threats to the nation, Sir Ken McCallum, the head of the UK’s intelligence service, MI5, warned that AI had the potential to ‘change the stakes’ on existing and even new bioweapons. To find out why, and how, Ian Sample speaks to Dr Tom Inglesby, director of the Johns Hopkins Center for Health Security and the Bloomberg School of Public Health. cluster_stories.title: US Moves to Bar China’s DeepSeek From Federal Agency Systems
cluster_stories.summary: The Trump administration barred civilian US government agencies from using products or services from Chinese artificial intelligence startup DeepSeek, citing a potential threat to national security from the company’s operations in China.
cluster_stories.headline: US BANS DEEPSEEK FROM GOVERNMENT... National Security Threat

cluster_stories.title: AI Tool That Hacked Korean Banks Was Used in Japan, GMO Says
cluster_stories.summary: The hackers who recently infiltrated some of Japan’s biggest companies used an AI tool developed in China and linked to a rash of breaches at South Korean banks last month, according to a Tokyo-based internet security firm.
cluster_stories.headline: CHINESE AI TOOL USED IN JAPAN BANK HACKS LINKED TO KOREA BREACHES

cluster_stories.title: US orders civilian federal agencies to remove DeepSeek from their systems
cluster_stories.summary: The Department of Homeland Security has ordered US civilian federal agencies to remove DeepSeek products from their IT systems and stop buying them, under a 2018 supply chain security law. The order covers third-party tools built on DeepSeek’s models, and cites the risk that sensitive data could be shared with the Chinese government. cluster_stories.headline: US ORDERS FEDERAL AGENCIES TO PURGE DEEPSEEK... DHS Invokes Security Law

cluster_stories.summary: Microsoft points the blame for ConnectWise's breach at a China-aligned hacker, which relied on AI agents to rapidly hack into thousands of its customers.
